findings.F1: Sense 1 definition says uncountable noun / not much instead of plural countable noun / not many, contradicting the rest of the entry.
findings.F2: Usage note gives less/least as the comparative and superlative of few instead of fewer/fewest.
findings.F3: Quite a few (a fairly large number) is listed only as a collocation under the small-number sense instead of being covered properly.
findings.F4: Adaptation grammar note duplicates the few/little countability fact given in the learner-error and compare notes.
findings.F5: Sense 2 example 'Could I borrow a few money?' is ungrammatical.
findings.F6: Inflections omit the real forms fewer and fewest.
findings.F7: Compare note marks illustrative phrases with double asterisks instead of single ones.
findings.F8: Usage note restates the few / a few contrast already given in the core idea and both explanations.
findings.F9: Neutral use of few after another determiner (every few days, the few people who came) is not covered.
findings.F10: Idiom 'few and far between' is missing from phrases.
